review_notes: Read the whole file and re-read the relevant ranges. The inner-product API (`charFun`) and the dual API (`charFunDual`) are proved separately, and several lemmas get the same proof twice. The main duplicates are `charFun_map_add_const`/`charFunDual_map_add_const` and `charFun_conv`/`charFunDual_conv`. I also saw that the `*_eq_prod_iff` and `*_eq_pi_iff` `mp` branches and the `charFunDual_prod'`/`charFunDual_pi'` proofs share a pattern, but they are short and mostly call existing lemmas, so I did not report them. Another, weaker overlap is `charFunDual_eq_charFun_map_one`, which is the `u = 1` case of `charFun_map_eq_charFunDual_smul`. I did not report it because the shared block is only a short `integral_map` computation. I did not compile anything. The replacement proofs are sketches. I did not look up the exact name or form of the `toDualMap` application lemma, so the sketches describe the rewrite rather than cite one.

findings.problem: `charFun_map_add_const` and `charFunDual_map_add_const` (lines 392–400) have the same proof, line for line. Each unfolds to an integral, pushes the measure through `integral_map` with two `fun_prop` side goals, pulls the constant out with `integral_mul_const`, merges the two exponentials with `Complex.exp_add`, then shows additivity of the phase (`inner_add_left` or `map_add`) followed by `ring`. The only difference is the additive phase map, `x ↦ ⟪x,t⟫` or `x ↦ L x`. The inner-product statement is the dual statement for `L = toDualMap ℝ E t`, a bridge the file already proves as `charFun_eq_charFunDual_toDualMap` (line 370). The same translation is not used here, so the translation shift argument is proved twice.
findings.proposed_change: Prove the shift lemma once, for `charFunDual`, which is the more general statement. Then derive `charFun_map_add_const` from it with `charFun_eq_charFunDual_toDualMap`, rewriting `charFun μ t` and `charFun (μ.map (· + r)) t` as `charFunDual` at `InnerProductSpace.toDualMap ℝ E t`. Finish with `charFunDual_map_add_const` and a `simp` that evaluates `toDualMap` at `r`, using `real_inner_comm` as in line 373. `charFun_map_const_add` then follows unchanged. This needs a small reorder: move `charFunDual_map_add_const` and `charFun_eq_charFunDual_toDualMap` before `charFun_map_add_const`, or move the `charFun` lemma into the `NormedSpace` section after them. Both lemmas have compatible hypotheses: `BorelSpace E` and a normed inner product space. `NormedSpace ℝ E` is available from the inner product structure.
findings.benefit: The measure-shift argument, with its `integral_map`, `integral_mul_const` and `exp_add` steps, is maintained in one place. A fix in one version, for example after a change to `integral_map` or `fun_prop` side goals, no longer has to be copied to the other. The inner-product lemma becomes a short corollary that shows its relation to the dual API.

findings.problem: `charFun_conv` and `charFunDual_conv` (lines 542–549) are proved by the same argument. Both unfold to an integral and apply `integral_conv`, then show integrability of the phase function by bounding it by the constant `1` through `(integrable_const (1 : ℝ)).mono (by fun_prop) (by simp)`. Both then split the exponential of a sum with `add_mul`, `Complex.exp_add`, `integral_const_mul` and `integral_mul_const`. The only variation is the additive phase map, `⟪·, t⟫` against `L`. The inner-product case is an instance of the dual case via `charFun_eq_charFunDual_toDualMap`, which the file already has, so the convolution-multiplicativity argument is duplicated.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one proof, for `charFunDual_conv`. Rewrite `charFun_conv` with `charFun_eq_charFunDual_toDualMap` on all three occurrences, `charFun (μ ∗ ν) t`, `charFun μ t` and `charFun ν t`, then close with `charFunDual_conv (InnerProductSpace.toDualMap ℝ E t)`. This needs `charFunDual_conv` and the bridge lemma moved before `charFun_conv`, or `charFun_conv` moved after them. Both lemmas sit under the same `[BorelSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E]` variables and `IsFiniteMeasure` assumptions, and `NormedSpace ℝ E` follows from `InnerProductSpace ℝ E`, so no hypotheses are lost. If the file layout must stay fixed, extract a private lemma stating that, for any additive measurable `φ : E → ℝ`, `∫ exp (φ x * I) ∂(μ ∗ ν) = (∫ exp (φ x * I) ∂μ) * (∫ exp (φ x * I) ∂ν)`, and use it in both.
findings.benefit: The integrability side condition and the sum-to-product computation are written once. The inner-product convolution theorem becomes a three-line corollary, and the file is shorter and easier to maintain.
